title: AWGN Mutual-Information Chain Rule I(X;Y) = h(Y) − h(Z)

problemStatement.formal: Y = X + Z,\quad X \perp Z \Rightarrow I(X;Y) = h(Y) - h(Y\mid X) = h(Y) - h(Z),
problemStatement.plain: The AWGN capacity entry currently assembles the capacity value $C = \tfrac12\log(1+P/N)$ from an *entropy difference* $h(Y) - h(Z)$ that is taken as a hypothesis. We want to make that difference operational: define the (differential) mutual information $I(X;Y)$ for the additive channel $Y = X + Z$ with independent noise, and prove the chain-rule decomposition $I(X;Y) = h(Y) - h(Y\mid X) = h(Y) - h(Z)$. Because conditioning on $X$ leaves only the noise, $h(Y\mid X) = h(Z)$; combined with the Gaussian entropy formula this upgrades the entry from an algebraic identity to the genuine operational capacity theorem.
